ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows two bracketed resonance structures for bisulfite with a double-headed arrow between them. In the left resonance structure, sulfur is double-bonded to the top oxygen, single-bonded to the left oxygen, and single-bonded to the oxygen that is bonded to H on the right. In the right resonance structure, sulfur is double-bonded to the left oxygen, single-bonded to the top oxygen, and still single-bonded to the oxygen bonded to H on the right. Reasoning: The task is to compare the three sulfur-oxygen bond lengths. Averaging the bond orders across the two resonance contributors gives: top S-O bond = (2 + 1)/2 = 1.5, left S-O bond = (1 + 2)/2 = 1.5, and S-OH bond = (1 + 1)/2 = 1. A higher bond order corresponds to a shorter bond, so the top and left S-O bonds are equal and shorter, while the S-OH bond is longer.

Use the text to focus on comparing the three S-O bonds. Therefore the bisulfite ion has two equal shorter S-O bonds and one longer S-O bond.
